claims.text: Lower-extremity superficial venous thrombosis ≤ 3 cm from the saphenofemoral junction: anticoagulate as for DVT for 6 weeks or longer.
claims.quote: In patients with lower extremity superficial venous thrombosis ≤ 3 cm from the saphenofemoral junction, treatment with anticoagulation as for a deep vein thrombosis for 6 weeks or longer is recommended

claims.text: > 3 cm from the junction but ≥ 5 cm long: fondaparinux (or rivaroxaban or an LMWH such as enoxaparin)
claims.quote: For patients with lower extremity superficial venous thrombosis that is > 3 cm from the saphenofemoral junction but ≥ 5 cm in length, treatment with fondaparinux (or, alternatively, rivaroxaban or a low molecular weight heparin

claims.text: Azole antifungals and protease inhibitors raise oral Xa inhibitor levels; certain antiseizure drugs and rifampin lower them.
claims.quote: azole antifungal therapy and protease inhibitors will increase oral factor Xa inhibitor levels, and certain antiseizure medications and rifampin will decrease oral factor Xa inhibitor levels

claims.text: Reversal: andexanet alfa (Andexxa) was indicated for life-threatening or uncontrolled bleeding on rivaroxaban or apixaban;
claims.quote: ANDEXXA is indicated for patients treated with rivaroxaban or apixaban, when reversal of anticoagulation is needed due to life-threatening or uncontrolled bleeding.
Andexxa will no longer be manufactured for or sold in the U.S. by AstraZeneca after December 22, 2025.

claims.text: If andexanet alfa is unavailable, 4-factor prothrombin complex concentrate may be considered.
claims.quote: If andexanet alfa is unavailable, 4-factor prothrombin complex concentrate may be considered.
claims.locator: Bleeding During Use of Anticoagulants: Anticoagulant reversal
